findings.message: update_permissions is described as 'Adds or updates permissions' but the actual implementation (and its REST API link 'Replace Content Permissions') overwrites all existing permissions — any rule not in the supplied list is deleted. This misleading description could cause callers to accidentally revoke permissions they didn't intend to remove.
findings.tp_fp_justification: The doc says 'Adds or updates permissions' but the REST API link directly references 'Replace Content Permissions' (replace_permissions_for_content), which overwrites all existing permissions. The description and the linked API are directly contradictory, and the inaccurate description could cause callers to accidentally revoke permissions not included in the supplied list.
findings.severity_justification: A misleading description of a permissions-modifying operation can lead to users inadvertently revoking access for principals not included in the call — a real security/correctness risk in production environments.
findings.category_justification: The issue is an inaccurate description in the documentation that contradicts the actual behavior of the underlying REST API endpoint.

findings.message: delete_dqw links to the wrong REST API anchor: '#delete_dqw_triggers' (Delete Quality Warning Triggers by Content). The actual implementation calls DELETE on /sites/{site_id}/dataQualityWarnings/datasource/{id}, which corresponds to '#delete_dqws' (Delete Data Quality Warning). The source code docstring for this method also confirms the correct anchor is '#delete_dqws'.
findings.tp_fp_justification: The description explicitly says 'Removes all data quality warnings' but the REST API link points to '#delete_dqw_triggers' (Delete Quality Warning Triggers by Content), which is a different endpoint. Data quality warnings and data quality warning triggers are distinct Tableau REST API concepts. The link and the description are internally inconsistent, and the correct anchor for deleting DQW instances would be '#delete_dqws'.
findings.severity_justification: A wrong REST API anchor in the docs is misleading for users trying to look up the underlying API, but does not affect runtime behavior. Low impact but a real documentation inaccuracy.
findings.category_justification: The issue is an incorrect REST API reference link in the documentation.

findings.message: In `datasources.delete_permission`, the parameter `capability_item` is described as being a `PermissionsRule` object. The name `capability_item` is misleading because a `PermissionsRule` defines permissions for a grantee (a user or group), not just a capability. A more accurate name would be `permission_rule`.
findings.tp_fp_justification: The parameter name `capability_item` appears in the actual method signature code block, indicating it is the real Python parameter name. Suggesting renaming it in the docs without changing the actual implementation would create inconsistency. This is a subjective naming preference about the underlying API design, not a documentation error — the docs accurately reflect the actual parameter name.
findings.severity_justification: Even if valid, this would be a minor naming style suggestion with no runtime impact.
findings.category_justification: The finding is about parameter naming style in the API.
